Gossamer Bio ( (GOSS) ) has shared an announcement.

On August 20, 2026, Gossamer Bio entered into a structured private placement of up to approximately $250 million, built around milestone-based pre-funded and approval-linked warrants to finance seralutinib’s path through U.S. regulatory review for pulmonary arterial hypertension. The deal, publicly announced on August 21, 2026, includes $150 million of committed capital, with $25 million expected at an initial closing on August 24, 2026 and $125 million upon FDA acceptance of the seralutinib NDA, plus up to $100 million from warrants exercisable only after FDA approval.

The financing, which features non-voting convertible preferred stock, lock-up provisions, beneficial ownership limits and a requirement for Nasdaq-mandated stockholder approval before common shares can be issued, brings in leading healthcare investors and existing shareholders to back Gossamer’s pulmonary hypertension franchise. Proceeds from the initial and second closings, combined with current cash reserves, are expected to fund operations into 2028 and support late-stage development and potential commercialization of seralutinib in PAH and PH-ILD, while leaving the ultimate level and timing of shareholder dilution dependent on future regulatory outcomes and warrant exercises.

Gossamer Bio, Inc. is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing seralutinib for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD). The San Diego-based company aims to become a leader in pulmonary hypertension therapies and improve outcomes for patients living with these severe cardiopulmonary conditions.

Gossamer’s strategy centers on advancing seralutinib through late-stage clinical development and regulatory review, following its recent reacquisition of worldwide rights to the drug. The company targets niche but high-need segments of the cardiovascular and respiratory market, using structured financings to support development, potential commercialization, and broader expansion in PAH and PH-ILD.

On August 20, 2026, Gossamer Bio entered into a structured securities purchase agreement for a private placement of up to approximately $250 million to fund seralutinib’s path through potential U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval in PAH. The transaction, announced publicly on August 21, 2026, includes $150 million of committed capital split between an initial $25 million closing expected on August 24, 2026 and a second $125 million closing contingent on FDA acceptance of the planned seralutinib new drug application in 2026, plus up to $100 million from approval-linked warrants.

The financing, which features pre-funded warrants, FDA approval-linked warrants and non-voting convertible preferred stock, draws participation from existing shareholders and prominent healthcare investors such as EcoR1 Capital, RA Capital Management and others, and is structured to align capital inflows with regulatory milestones while imposing lock-up and stockholder-approval conditions on common stock issuance. Gossamer expects that proceeds from the initial and second closings, together with existing cash resources, will fund operations into 2028 and support clinical development and potential commercialization of seralutinib in PAH and PH-ILD, with implications for shareholder dilution tied to future conversions and warrant exercises subject to Nasdaq and stockholder approval.
